incumbent.name: Todd Huston
incumbent.summary: Todd Huston, a Fishers Republican first elected in 2012, has been Speaker of the Indiana House since March 2020, when he succeeded retiring Speaker Brian Bosma; House Republicans re-elected him as speaker in 2022 and 2024 {caucus_huston} {caucus_speaker_2024}. As speaker he leads a chamber with a 70-member Republican supermajority and serves on the Joint Rules Committee and the Legislative Council {caucus_huston}. The House Republican caucus continued to identify him as speaker in September 2026 {caucus_gas_tax}.
record: Leadership: Speaker of the House since 2020; member of the Joint Rules Committee and Legislative Council {caucus_huston} {caucus_speaker_2024}.

2025 session: The House Republican caucus lists the session's main laws under his speakership as the two-year budget (HEA 1001), K-12 deregulation (HEA 1002), health care pricing transparency (HEA 1003), nonprofit hospital rules (HEA 1004), housing infrastructure (HEA 1005), a board to review prosecutors who decline to enforce laws (HEA 1006) and energy policy (HEA 1007) {caucus_session_2025}. Huston authored HEA 1008, allowing Illinois counties that voted to secede to join Indiana {caucus_session_2025}.

April 10, 2025: The House passed an amended SEA 1, the property-tax law, 65-29, with Huston voting yes {rc_sea1_433}; he said "Two-thirds of Hoosier homeowners will see a lower bill in 2026 than they did in 2025" {caucus_sea1}. April 25, 2025: Voted yes as the House adopted the budget conference report (HEA 1001), 66-27 {rc_hb1001_576}.

Nov. 18, 2025: Said House Republicans had the votes for mid-decade congressional redistricting and hoped the Senate would join in passing a map giving Republicans all nine seats {caucus_redistricting}. Dec. 5, 2025: Voted yes as the House passed HB 1032, 57-41 {rc_hb1032_28}; the Senate rejected it 31-19 on Dec. 11 {wndu_senate_rejects}.

2026 session: The caucus lists the House Republican agenda bills as HEA 1001 (housing regulation), HEA 1002 (utility performance targets), HEA 1003 (consolidating state boards) and HEA 1004 (K-12 deregulation); Huston said the session "was focused on affordability for Hoosier families and streamlining government" {caucus_session_2026}.
April 2026: Issued a statement on HEA 1303 (child alert system) and HEA 1408 (social media safeguards for minors), laws inspired by the death of Fishers teen Hailey Buzbee {caucus_buzbee}.

2022: Left his job as a College Board senior vice president after the Indiana Democratic Party called him "a walking conflict of interest" as the House advanced education bills; Huston said he was "focused on a strong, successful finish to this legislative session" {aibb_collegeboard}.

race_context: House District 37 covers part of Hamilton County, including Fishers {caucus_huston}.
May 5, 2026 primaries: Huston was unopposed for the Republican nomination; Lauren Cole won the Democratic nomination with 2,167 votes (55.2%) to 1,757 (44.8%) for Joel Levi {wiki_2026}.

Key differences: Huston has led the House Republican agenda on property-tax changes, the 2025 budget and the 2025 redistricting effort {caucus_session_2025} {caucus_redistricting}; Cole says she is focused on public school funding, working families and government transparency {reporter_cole}.
No debate or forum for this race was found.

candidates.summary: Todd Huston is the Republican incumbent and Speaker of the Indiana House, first elected in 2012 {caucus_huston}. As speaker he has led House action on the 2025 property-tax law and budget and the 2025 redistricting bill {caucus_session_2025} {caucus_redistricting}.
background: Bachelor's degree in political science from Indiana University; former Hamilton Southeastern school board member and Fishers Plan Commission member; appointed by Gov. Mitch Daniels to the State Board of Education and the Indiana Education Roundtable; lives in Fishers {caucus_huston}.
Was a senior vice president at the College Board until 2022 {aibb_collegeboard}.
path_to_ballot: Unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary {wiki_2026}.

items: Said SEA 1 delivered "robust property tax relief for Hoosiers" {caucus_sea1}; said that between property tax relief and income tax cuts, Hoosiers would see about $600 million in tax cuts in 2026 and $700 million in 2027 {caucus_session_2025}.

Said the 2026 laws "expand Indiana's housing supply and drive down costs of homeownership" {caucus_session_2026}; said "The best way to reduce cost burdens on Hoosiers is to roll back regulation and bureaucracy" {caucus_agenda_2026}.
Listed HEA 1002 (2026), which sets performance targets for utilities on cost and reliability, as a caucus priority {caucus_agenda_2026}.

Supported mid-decade congressional redistricting in 2025, saying he hoped Congress would bar the practice but that Indiana should use every available legal tool in the meantime {caucus_redistricting}.
Fox59 reported that Huston had repeatedly expressed disinterest in a 2025 bill to legalize recreational marijuana {fox59_hb1630}.

on_incumbent: Is the current officeholder. No statements by Huston about Cole were found.
plans: Announced a 2026 House Republican agenda aimed at keeping Indiana "a low cost of living state" through housing, utility, government-consolidation and education bills {caucus_agenda_2026}.
endorsements_finance: No 2026 endorsements or fundraising figures were found.
gaps: Current Publishing's March 2026 Q&A with the District 37 candidates returned 403 and was not read.
No statement from Huston after the Senate's Dec. 11, 2025 rejection of HB 1032 was found.

candidates.summary: Lauren Cole, a first-time candidate who works in health care, is the Democratic nominee {reporter_cole}. She focuses on public education, working families and transparency in state government {reporter_cole}.
background: The Reporter describes her as a senior coordinator in medical affairs at LabCorp Biopharma {reporter_cole}; BallotReady lists her as a molecular technologist supervisor at Patients Choice Laboratories since 2022 {br_cole}.
path_to_ballot: Announced in February 2026 {reporter_cole}; won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary with 55.2% over Joel Levi {wiki_2026}.

items: Has criticized underfunding of public schools and says every child should have access to a high-quality education {reporter_cole}.
Says she is running "to represent the people who work hard every day and just want a fair shot" {reporter_cole}.
Says "government should be a window, not a black box" and that people deserve to know "where their tax dollars go" {reporter_cole}.

on_incumbent: No direct statements about Huston were found. She has said, "I'm not running to represent the powerful" {reporter_cole}.
plans: Says "This campaign is about bringing the power back to the people where it belongs" {reporter_cole}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or fundraising figures were found.
gaps: Her campaign Facebook page could not be read; no campaign website found.
Current Publishing's candidate filing story and March 2026 Q&A returned 403 and were not read.
Search snippets said she completed Ballotpedia's candidate survey and lists a 2020 Earlham College degree; Ballotpedia could not be loaded, so these are unverified.
Her employer differs between The Reporter (LabCorp Biopharma) and BallotReady (Patients Choice Laboratories).
